Players are welcomed into the Imperial Hatchery to construct the ideal dragon-arium. While placing tiles to make connected domains, make full use of elements circling the player board — an innovative resource mechanism — to breathe life into your dragons. The game is played over twelve rounds. Each player drafts a tile with one or two land types, placing it to build their dragonarium out...and up! Then choose one of the land types just placed to activate an element token (fire, water, wind, and light) circling the player board. As the token passes by a row or column, it provides the energy needed to hatch the dragons found on placed tiles. Once ready to hatch, place a tile on top, releasing it into the dragonarium. The land where the dragon nests, however, allows players to further connect domains as the tile now shares the element of the placed dragon. Aside from being a robust (more traditional) spatial puzzle, Dragonarium challenges your timing for when and where to release your dragons so as to interweave their domains. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Key Concepts 3 Tile & Component References 4 Gameplay 5 End of Game & Scoring 6 Solo Objective Take on the role of an imperial hatchery official and build the most magnificent Dragonarium. Select territory tiles, strategically place them outwards and/or upwards, and use the elements of fire, water, and air to hatch dragons. The player with the most valuable domains after 12 rounds wins. Key Concepts Domains: As territory tiles are placed, domains expand both outwards and upwards. A domain is a continuous group of connected squares (edge adjacent) of the same territory type: fire (red), water (blue), air (green), and royal (yellow). Grey is not a territory type. When moving the assistant and for final scoring (below), only consider the largest domain of each Territory type. Tile & Component References Territory Tiles: Each tile consists of two squares . There are three kinds of squares: With a territory type, namely fire, water, air or royal; and require two element stones to hatch. Without a territory type (grey); require one element stone to hatch; and provide one pillar. Without a territory type (grey); and provide two pillars. Dragon Eggs: They are depicted on the squares. They require element stones and then need to be covered by a later placed territory tile to hatch. Dragons: Once hatched, a dragon nests on any square. That square now counts as having two types: the original square type (if any) AND the dragon's type. Pillar Tiles: Used as supports to place territory tiles flat on higher levels. Gameplay The game lasts 12 rounds. Each round consists of player turns and replenishing the planning site (market). A turn includes three steps: Draft and Place a Tile: Choose one tile from the planning site. Place it on level 1 (player board) or higher if able. There are no adjacency rules. Tiles on higher levels must lay flat (may use as many pillars needed for your supply to support one square). Rules: Tiles cannot be placed on top of squares not ready to hatch (still require element stones) or on squares with dragons. Hatch Dragons: If the placed tile covers a square that has all its required element stones, its dragon hatches. Take the corresponding dragon and place it on any square (including level 0 of the Dragonarium player board). The square with a Dragon now counts as also having the Territory type of the placed Dragon. Move the Assistant: Choose one element (fire, water, or air). Count the number of squares in your largest domain of the chosen element and move your assistant exactly that many steps clockwise. At each step, place one stone of the element onto a matching empty egg space in that row or column.
